head: 693a9fb44e7d6effa20f988217524c61553f95fe
body:
Depends on #327 and #328. Fixes #322 and #329; adds the manual empty-cache controls requested in #96. The branch contains both independent correctness prerequisites so it compiles and can be tested today; rebase after they merge.

Resolve each memory type's sizing once using explicit CPU accessibility: Vulkan HOST_VISIBLE, D3D12 standard/custom CPU page properties, and Metal Shared versus Private. This describes access, not physical RAM versus VRAM. Use the resolved maximum for the shared/dedicated threshold and grow to fit the resource, counting occupied shared blocks.

Keep one bounded empty cache per type (at most min(2*minimum, maximum)), with aggregate Vulkan retention bounded by the physical heap. Expose cached_capacity(), trim() and trim_to(bytes) using cached indices without scanning historical slots. Under typed memory pressure, reuse compatible blocks, reclaim empty caches and retry, then reduce shared block sizes toward the aligned resource floor. Fatal and allocation-count failures do not cause size retries. Metal uses a conservative exact-floor attempt and commits pending residency removals.

Validation on final 693a9fb (test-only successor of measured b620867): 54 std and 10 no_std library tests; strict Clippy, rustdoc and formatting; actual Rust 1.71 std / 1.81 no_std consumers; Apple ARM/Intel cross-compilation. Six final-source native harness processes match all 60 prior normal allocation-plan cells. Historical seven-policy and downstream comparisons, raw data and reproducer: https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/allocator-reconciliation-20261128. Historical timings are not new final-source timings.

Limits: no Apple runtime validation; source-confirmed Metal selection/platform defects #330 and #331 remain separate. The historical integrated wgpu run has 2,184 passes and 23 failures/aborts, not a passing full native suite. Twenty-two reproduce on pristine upstream; the remaining DX12 multiview behavior depends on executable basename and remains unresolved (gfx-rs/wgpu#8645). wgpu cross-pool recovery also needs a real release of these APIs (gfx-rs/wgpu#11145); no release number or production override is proposed.

head: 8b08388331e0479c965cd602557bbf8feade500c
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Traverse-Research/gpu-allocator/issues/325.

Return reserved suballocations when placed-resource options or native creation fail. Drop a partial native resource before returning its backing allocation. Convert null-success outputs to internal errors. This is independent of #323 and does not change sizing or caching.

Validation: five COM-stub tests using the public allocator constructor pass; four fail on main. Formatting, strict all-target Clippy and a Rust 1.71 consumer build pass on Windows. No physical OOM is required by the tests.

head: 99e3979dae3a7c4e8300c33cea681a175f1b3747
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Traverse-Research/gpu-allocator/issues/326; addresses this allocator's portion of #125.

Cap every native block to its selected heap, reject impossible requests before the driver call, guard owned allocation count, and try compatible types once in preference order only after recoverable failures. Preserve fatal allocation/mapping errors. Exclude AMD device-coherent types because device feature enablement is unavailable. Publish a new block only after its first suballocation succeeds.

Independent of #323: existing sizing threshold, growth and empty-cache policy remain in place. External native allocations still require caller coordination for the device-wide count limit.

Validation: ten public-constructor driver-stub tests pass (nine fail against main); strict std/no_std Clippy, formatting, Rust 1.71 std and Rust 1.81 no_std consumer builds pass. Normal failed-map cleanup already existed; null-success handling is defensive.

## Connections

Related to #9818. Independent of #11130 and new gpu-allocator APIs.

## Description

Create and upload the default external-texture parameter buffer when a TextureView is first bound as an external texture. Idle devices avoid the unused buffer, staging upload and retained upload heap.

Initialize before taking the snatchable read lock; upgrade the queue outside the OnceCell initializer so queue destruction cannot re-enter initialization. Preserve concurrent first use, pending-write setup, zero initialization and binding after queue drop.

## Testing

Rebased on bfa9aff; runtime source and Cargo.lock match the previous PR head (only upstream CI changed). Final independent checks: formatting, strict all-target/all-feature core Clippy, Rust 1.95 compilation, and 41 focused harness cases passing: 29 executed checks and 12 Vulkan feature-unsupported entries. Physical DX12, bundled WARP and API validation cover first use, concurrency, submit and queue-drop regressions. Vulkan first-use external-texture coverage is unavailable on this adapter.

The initial focused attempt had12 adapter-matching failures because its WARP DLL did not match the metadata; the corrected runtime rerun passes all41. Both attempts are preserved. The historical integrated full native suite remains non-green (2184/2207, 23 failures/aborts,18 profile exclusions); this is not a new full-suite pass. Local DX12 multiview behavior remains unresolved; Apple runtime validation of the experimental allocator changes remains outstanding. Raw comparisons, exact source reuse proof and checks: https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/allocator-reconciliation-20261128

## Connections

Related to #9818. Independent of #11129. Resource-creation rollback is tracked separately in #11142; cross-pool recovery is blocked on released allocator APIs in #11145.

## Description

Route TRANSIENT DX12 allocations to a separate allocator, mirroring Vulkan's lifetime separation. Long-lived buffers then do not keep transient heaps occupied. Use the existing quarter-sized minima with the 4 MiB floor, preserve maxima, record pool ownership for frees, and combine reports with corrected allocation ranges.

Retain this split with the improved allocator: the measured single-pool alternative retains 48 MiB more in both repeated uploads and sustained rendering. Cross-pool reclamation can follow when its allocator APIs are released; this PR keeps the current registry dependency.

## Testing

Rebased on bfa9aff; runtime source and Cargo.lock match the previous head (only upstream CI changed). Formatting, strict all-target/all-feature HAL Clippy and actual Rust 1.95 compilation pass. The sizing regression passes; transient lifetime checks pass independently on physical DX12, WARP and Vulkan.

Historical comparisons use five processes per cell; the integrated full native suite remains non-green (2184/2207, 23 failures/aborts,18 profile exclusions). These timings are historical, and the focused checks do not constitute a new full-suite pass. Local DX12 multiview behavior remains unresolved; Apple runtime validation of the experimental allocator changes remains outstanding. A separate registry-compatible pool/rollback integration also typechecks on Rust 1.95. ## Description

Return reserved allocations when native buffer, texture or acceleration-structure creation fails. Drop any partial native resource before freeing its allocation, and roll back allocations on SetName errors. Count memory only after creation completes. Treat success-with-null output as an error.

Fixes https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/issues/11150. Keeps the rendering/presentation regression for #10410.

## Description

Accept both Success and Suboptimal acquisitions in surface_configure. The public API documents Suboptimal as successfully acquired and usable; rejecting it prevents this test from reaching view creation, rendering and presentation on affected systems. Other acquisition errors still fail the test.

## Testing

The original Success-only assertion fails in clean-upstream and standalone rollback full runs. This test-only fix passes three Vulkan and three DX12 repetitions on Windows/Intel Arc, formatting, strict test-target Clippy and actual Rust 1.95 compilation.

The required full native integration run with the independent DX12 creation rollback completed: 2180/2202 passing harness entries and 22 failures/aborts/timeouts, plus 18 profile exclusions. The surface regression passes in that run. The full suite remains non-green; all failures and their controls are recorded in the linked evidence. Earlier full runs are not green: ray/mesh failures and unresolved multiview behavior are documented separately. Local Apple runtime validation was unavailable.
